NOON REPORT - MV TORMAR SPRING
Date/time: 26 Jan 2025 1200 (ship's time UTC)
Position: 50-50.2N 031-32.2W
Distance run last 24h: 231.3 nm
Average speed last 24h: 12.5 kn
ROB VLSFO: 1019.0 t
ROB MGO: 94.5 t
Consumption last 24h: VLSFO 18.8 t, MGO 0.1 t
Next port: Sept-Iles
ETA Sept-Iles: 2025-01-31 1100 UTC
ETA based on: 12.5 kn
Remarks: Main engine stopped 0610-1140 UTC: low lube oil pressure alarm. Cause traced to a blocked strainer; strainer cleaned, pressure normal, engine restarted and passage resumed. Average speed over 18.5 h steaming. Fuel used during stoppage: VLSFO 1.1 t (generators and boiler).

Master MV TORMAR SPRING

result.result:
The Master's ETA of 2025-01-31T11:00:00Z to Sept-Iles is consistent (within the 2-hour tolerance of the distance-to-go calculation), and no charter party ETA notice is due — the next notice tier is 3 days before arrival and the vessel is about 5 days out; notices go to the agent.

Regarding the stoppage, check_stoppage confirms the main engine stop of 26 January 2025, 06:10–11:40 UTC (5.5 hours) agrees with the noon report: the reported speed over the remaining 18.5 steaming hours reproduces the distance run exactly. The stop was a machinery breakdown (low lube oil pressure from a blocked strainer), explained in the remarks, so no query to the Master is needed.

Under the CP off-hire clause, time lost through a breakdown of machinery is off hire, so this stop falls within the clause. The off-hire statement figures are simulated: hire deducted $2,177.08 for 5.5 hours at $9,500/day; 1.1 t VLSFO at $660 for the owners' account; total $2,837.08.

The operator should decide whether to put the ship off hire for 2025-01-26T06:10:00Z to 2025-01-26T11:40:00Z and notify the owner. On a yes: (a) a voyage management system entry for the off-hire period, and (b) an e-mail to the owner's vessel technical management (Tormar Bulk Carriers) giving the period and reason and asking for the engine log extract for the stop.

Dear Owner,

MV TORMAR SPRING was off-hire from 2025-01-26T06:10:00Z to 2025-01-26T11:40:00Z (5.5 hours) due to a main engine breakdown.

The low lube oil pressure alarm was traced to a blocked strainer. The strainer was cleaned, pressure returned to normal, the engine was restarted, and passage resumed.

Please provide the engine log extract for the stop.

Best regards,
Operations
